examples.code:
### Accordion align

In rare cases, you may need to specify the alignment of the icon in the
accordion. You can use the `align` prop to specify the side where the icon
should be placed.

_Note: This prop must not be used to create a tree view or set of nested
accordions._

```jsx
<Accordion align="start">
  <AccordionItem title="Panel A">Panel A</AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Panel B">Panel B</AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Panel C">Panel C</AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

examples.code:
## References

### Why is interactive content in a heading considered an accessibility violation?

When using the `title` prop from `Accordion`, it is possible to render arbitrary
markup within the accordion header. The accordion header itself is rendered as a
`<button>` and is considered an interactive element.

If you render an interactive element inside this header, then it becomes nested
inside the `<button>`. Common examples of this are buttons or links. Rendering
interactive content inside the accordion heading is not reachable via a keyboard
or screen reader.

entries.guidance: Use accordions for independently expandable sections in dense product screens, not hierarchical navigation that requires a real tree pattern. The inspected docs allow changing disclosure-icon side with align but explicitly reject using it to fake a tree view. Treat the title as one interactive button's label: place edit, help, download or overflow actions outside that heading. Separate those actions spatially on the same baseline with restrained dividers, so a functional row does not become a decorative card. Give the body a readable line length and preserve keyboard focus visibility. The second excerpt is an actionable accessibility constraint, not source to render. Full Apache license is retained; no IBM fonts, pictograms, icons or Sass bundle were copied.
entries.summary: Carbon warns that accordion headings are buttons: nested links or buttons are unreachable for keyboard or screen-reader users. Icon alignment must not be used to simulate a tree view.
entries.title: Carbon accordion anatomy — avoid nested actions and false tree views

entries.guidance: Adapt Root/Item/ItemTrigger/ItemContent/ItemBody to real settings: identify the setting in the title and summarize its current value or consequence on a short second line. The story uses Stack gap="1" and Text fontSize="sm" color="fg.muted" to establish hierarchy without another bordered card. Replace "Click to expand" with input-neutral, informative copy, and replace LoremIpsum with actual content. Use stable item IDs as React keys, not the example index. Check muted-text contrast in both themes, focus visibility and wrapping at narrow widths. Let application typography and spacing set the rhythm rather than repeating marketing tiles. The excerpt depends on Chakra and surrounding items data; it is not standalone code.
entries.summary: An accordion trigger stacks a title with smaller muted subtext, while the body lives in ItemContent/ItemBody. Useful for compact preferences and setup screens.

entries.guidance: Choose multiple=true for independent filters or reference sections, and a single controlled value for mutually exclusive setup panels. The inspected props include loop for arrow-key wraparound and order for h2–h6 wrappers around controls; match order to the document outline, not font size. The default transition duration is 200ms: derive motion from the product and provide an appropriate reduced-motion alternative. Use separated or contained variants only when grouping is meaningful; a dense settings page often needs simple rows rather than rounded containers everywhere. Maintain value types when switching between single and multiple modes. Excerpts describe an internal prop contract and defaults, not a complete composition or installed dependency. These props alone do not guarantee accessibility.
entries.summary: Accordion props expose single/multiple disclosure, controlled state, arrow-key looping, transition duration and semantic heading order. Choose disclosure behavior deliberately rather than copying a generic FAQ.
entries.title: Mantine accordion controls — heading order and disclosure density

entries.guidance: Start with clear text commands, adding a leading icon only when it improves scanning. Reserve trailing visuals for meaningful secondary cues, not repeated decorative badges. ItemPlayground passes selectionVariant to ActionList and selected/active state to the item; distinguish current navigation from selected choices instead of painting both alike. Match row heights, icon alignment and separators to the product, preserving a visible focus target for each interactive row. Short command lists often need no card shadow. These are partial stories with omitted imports and arguments; verify actual routing, keyboard behavior and installed Primer APIs.

entries.guidance: Use React Aria behavior as a contract for an existing React overlay, not a reason to rebuild focus logic from a snippet. Wire title and container props together; alertdialog descriptions have a separate slot and role-specific handling. The inspected implementation delays initial focus while isEntering is true, preserves focus already inside, and enables overlay focus containment, with Safari/VoiceOver workarounds. Retain library behavior rather than copying its timeout in isolation. Keep entry motion brief, honor reduced motion, and make hierarchy readable without animation. Use a product-specific heading and consequence text rather than an ornamental modal hero. This is internal source, not a standalone public import example; verify the installed public hook API. Full Apache license and NOTICE are retained. No Spectrum icon package, font, logo, dependency or notice outbound link was fetched or bundled.
entries.summary: The inspected useDialog contract exposes dialogProps, titleProps and alert-dialog contentProps, with isEntering delaying focus until entry animation completes. A behavior reference for custom branded overlays.

entries.guidance: Upstream states Shoelace is sunset with no active development. Use this only as historical design/API guidance or to maintain an existing Shoelace application; do not select it as a new dependency based on this archive. In the inspected React example, onSlAfterHide resets open state so user dismissal remains synchronized, the footer slot carries the close button, and --width sets dialog size. Replace the generic label and filler with a concrete heading and content. The 50vw example is not a mobile-safe guarantee: choose a content-based maximum and narrow-screen width with safe margins, then test long content, focus return and keyboard dismissal. Preserve existing typography instead of importing a whole new theme. React adapters/custom elements remain uninstalled; no script tags or rendered media are included.
entries.summary: A historical Shoelace React dialog synchronizes open state via onSlAfterHide, places its close action in the footer slot and exposes a --width property. Useful for maintaining existing component-based sites.
entries.title: Shoelace legacy dialogs — controlled visibility and width tokens
